translation:
Among the seven honest-looking thieves, the ten avatars were named first, and Vaikunth is counted second. It will come as a surprise to hear that Vaikunth — the very abode people pine and die for — is called a thief along with the others. These "honest" thieves are called thieves precisely because they appear supreme to the world's unwise people, yet relying on them does not bring about our liberation. So we named the ten avatars as the first thief, but on closer look all seven of these thieves are, in one way or another, counted as avatars themselves. Among the twenty-four avatars, Vaikunth too is counted as an avatar. Besides those twenty-four, other avatars of God are also recognized. Among these, the third thief — Omkar — is counted as an avatar too, regarded as the sound-avatar (nadavatar). The fourth thief, the one dwelling in every heart (ghat-ghat), is the notion "I am Brahman" (aham brahm); a portion of the divine essence resides in every body. The fifth, Sanakadik, is counted among the twenty-four avatars. The sixth is Ekadashi. When God grew angry in order to slay the demon Madhukaitabh, a maiden appeared from that anger, and her name was Ekadashi; thus Ekadashi too is counted as an avatar of God. The seventh is the Ganga, called Vishnu-Padodaki (water from Vishnu's feet). During the Sanakadik avatar — since the Sanakadik sages were themselves an avatar of God — when God's foot struck their sweat-filled water-pot (kamandal), the stream that flowed from it was called the Ganga; thus the Ganga too is counted as part of that same avatar of God.

In the detailed discussion of the seven honest-looking thieves, Omkar, Ekadashi, and Ganga have been explained at length, while Vaikunth, Sanakadik, and the thief dwelling in every heart have only been mentioned in passing. Let us now look at what flaw lies within these. Vaikunth, being renowned as the abode of God, spreads its attraction among people, yet no one recognizes the fault hidden within it.

Vaikunth means the abode of Vishnu, the dwelling place of Vishnu. It is said that in the lower region of Satyalok, Vishnulok, and Golok there lies Vaikunthlok as one of its parts. The spiritual meaning of Vaikunth is that the intellect remains unblunted (akunth) through all religious observances. (Jagdish notebook no. 264, page 293)

Kshirpayonidhi — the Kshirsagar, the ocean of milk. Some scholars also call the Kshirsagar "Shvetdwip" (the White Island). Shvetdwip is the gateway to Vaikunth. Another name for Vaikunth is "Vyapi Vaikunth" (the all-pervading Vaikunth).

In the imperishable, all-pervading Vaikunth, the tree of the Vedas sprouts from the seed of the Pranav (the syllable Om). From this it appears that Brahma, who emerged from the navel-lotus of God reclining in the Kshirsagar, uttered the sound Om, and from that seed the Vedas were composed. This is why we do not accept this Vaikunth possessed of the Omkar-principle.

God's avatar exists in the form of Vaikunth. In the Raivat Manvantar, God took an avatar named "Vaikunth", born from the womb of Vaikuntha, wife of Shubhra. It is said that this same God then created Vaikunthlok. The Bhagavatam, in Canto 8, Chapter 5–6, verse 4, states that the wife of the sage Shubhra was named Vikuntha. From her womb, God himself, through his own portion (amsha), took an avatar named Vaikunth, together with the finest of the gods. Pleased by the prayer of Goddess Lakshmi, he then fashioned the abode of Vaikuntha for her.

Register no. 452, page 73, states that there are 108 Vaikunths on earth, and five other Vaikunths besides.

1. Kshirsagar Vaikunth — _Jab Shrimannarayan nidraki prerna karte hai tab Brahma nidravash swapnavasthako prapt hote hai aur tab Narayanki icchase jagat jalarpan hota hai jise naimitya pralay kahte hai - uska karan Kshirsagar Vaikunth hai_ (When Shrimannarayan induces sleep, Brahma falls into a dream-state under its sway, and by Narayan's will the world is then submerged in water — this is called the naimittika pralaya, incidental dissolution — and its cause is the Kshirsagar Vaikunth.)

2. Ramavaikunth — _jahan Sanakadikne Jay-Vijayko shaap diya tha_ (where Sanakadik cursed Jay and Vijay.)

3. Karan Vaikunth — _jahan mahapralayme prakriti purush samyatako prapt hone hai, jahan teeno gun aur panch tattva sam hai. Jab wahi purush Mahavishnu iccha karte hai tab phir jagat waisa hi ho jata hai_ (where, at the time of the great dissolution, Prakriti and Purush attain equilibrium, where the three gunas and the five elements are in balance; when that same Purush, Mahavishnu, wills it, the world comes into being again just as before.)

4. _Vaikunth Mahabhagvane chatuvyuh Vasudev Purush Prakritipar jahan virajman hai_ (Vaikunth — where the great Lord, in his fourfold [chaturvyuha] form as Vasudev-Purush, is enthroned upon Prakriti.)

5. _Padvaikunth. Yeh Virajapar hai_ (Padvaikunth — this lies beyond the river Viraja.)

Kalyan magazine, register 19, page 135 — Pandharpur: _is sthanko bhakt Bhuvaikunth athva Dakshin Dwarawati bhi kahte hai_ (devotees also call this place Bhu-Vaikunth, or the southern Dwarka [Dakshin Dwarawati].)

Register no. 452, page 199, states:

_Vaikunth vah hai jahan Jay-Vijayko shaap mila, Mahavaikunth vah hai jahan Shri Krishna aur Arjun mare hue Brahmanputroko lene gaye aur Kshirsagar vah hai jahan Brahmadik avatarke liye prarthana karte hai. (Skandh 10, Adhyay 1, Shlok 19-20) Devoke sahit Brahmajika Kshirsagar jana aur avatar dharan karneke liye prarthana karna yeh sab ekpad us lila vibhutime hota hai. Tripadvibhutime archiradi margse sushumnanadi dwara mukt hokar hi janeka adhikar hai. Kaushitaki Upanishadme vistarse iska varnan kiya hai_ (Vaikunth is the place where Jay and Vijay received the curse; Mahavaikunth is the place where Shri Krishna and Arjun went to fetch the dead sons of the brahmin; and Kshirsagar is where Brahma and the other gods go to pray for an avatar [Bhagavatam, Canto 10, Chapter 1, verses 19–20]. Brahma's going to the Kshirsagar with the gods, and praying there for an avatar to be taken — all of this occurs within that one quarter [ekapad] of the Lord's manifested glory. The three-quarter glory [tripad vibhuti] may be reached only by the liberated, through the archiradi path via the sushumna channel. The Kaushitaki Upanishad describes this in detail.)

_Iti sambhashya bhagavan arjunena saheshwarah, divyam swaratham asthaya pratichim disham avishamat_ (Thus having conversed, the Lord, together with Ishwar and Arjun, mounted the divine chariot and set out toward the west) — from here up to verse 57 the earthly Vaikunthdham is described. After this comes the account of the reverent exchange of greetings with the Lord of Vaikunth, the return to Dwarka bearing the brahmin's sons, and Arjun's astonishment at Shri Krishna's glory. This Vaikunth lies beyond the Lokalok mountain, beyond darkness, above the pure waters.

_Ramavaikunth ke dwarke sameep Dhruvjika nivas sthal hai - Atha tasmat paratah trayodasha-laksha-yojanantaro yat tad Vishnoh paramam padam abhivandati yatraha mahabhagvato Dhruva_, and so on (Near the gate of Ramavaikunth lies the dwelling place of Dhruvji — "Beyond that, at a distance of thirteen lakh yojanas, lies that supreme abode of Vishnu, which the great devotee Dhruv reverently worships.")

In the Bhagavatam, Canto 8, first half, in the account of the Raivat Manvantar, verses 4–5 and others make it clear that Lord Vaikunth, son of Vikuntha, manifested Ramavaikunth at the prayer of Lakshmiji. The going there of the Sanakadik brahmarshis, and their cursing of Jay and Vijay, is the story of Ramavaikunth.

Register no. 449, page 49, states:

_Vishnu avatarse Vaikunth Dham, Shrimannarayanavatarse Kshirshayi Vaikunth aur paratpar Parabrahm Samavatarse Saket Dham. Aagam-samhitao ke siddhantanusar Vaikunth sabse uncha swargko kahte hai, Vaikunthme Ishwarka sayujya prapt karta hai_ (From the Vishnu avatar comes Vaikunth Dham; from the Shrimannarayan avatar comes Kshirshayi ["ocean-reclining"] Vaikunth; and from the transcendent Parabrahm's Sama avatar comes Saket Dham. According to the doctrine of the Agam Samhitas, Vaikunth is called the highest heaven, and in Vaikunth one attains sayujya — union of identity with God.)

Thus, among the four kinds of liberation, one who attains the sarupya-sayujya kind of liberation reaches Vaikunth. But Jivanji rejected all four kinds of liberation. One who attains liberation there is granted four arms just like God's own — but by becoming like God, by becoming non-dual (advait) with him, one does not obtain prem-bhakti (loving devotion). Moreover, God does not dwell in a Vaikunth devoid of loving devotion. It is said in the Pancharatra:

_Naaham vasami vaikunthe yoginam hridaye na cha, madbhakta yatra gayanti tatra tishthami Narada_ (O Narada! I do not dwell in Vaikunth, nor even in the hearts of yogis — but wherever my devotees sing devotional songs, there I dwell.)

_Na Hari vaikunthama, na Vrindavandham, jahan santki mandali, uhan milat hai Ram_ (Lord Ram does not dwell in Vaikunth, nor even in Vrindavan-dham — but wherever the devotional gathering of saints takes place, there Ram is met.)

_Na Hari vaikunthme, jogi hirde nahi, gyaani harijan hari tahan, dooja thor nahi._ ||19|| (Gyaniji Maharaj says: God does not dwell in Vaikunth, nor in the hearts of yogis — but wherever there is a devotee of Hari, there Hari dwells; nowhere else.)

_Satjug treta Jivana, vaikunth hamaro vaas, dwapar Gokul vasu, kaljug jahan nijdas._ ||41|| (Jivandasji Maharaj says God declares: In Satyug and Treta my dwelling was in Vaikunth, and in Dwapar I resided in Gokul, but in Kaliyug I dwell wherever my innermost devotees are.)

Raga Asavari:

_Narad santan jivan mero, man karam vachan bhajai je moko, to bohor na aave fero. (tek)
Vaikunthme vaaso nahi mero, Dwaravati na hoi,
jahan mero sant gaave, tahan mai nachu, santanko mukh joi._ ||1||
_Maira sant bhukha to mai bhukha, sant jamai mai jeemu,
jahan mero sant sauve, tahan mai jaagu, santan mahe ramu._ ||2||
_Sakal tirath santke charane charane, Lakshmi tanki dasi,
kaam krodh lobh moh maya, e charau karat khavasi._ ||3||
_Kahet Kabir suno bhai santo, e Harike mukhki vani,
Narad pratye santko mahima, te gaayo Sarangvani._ ||4||

(God told Narada: O Narada, the saints are my very life; those who worship me in mind, word, and deed will not come back again into the round of birth and death. [Refrain] I do not dwell in Vaikunth, nor in Dwarka; but wherever my saint sings, there I dance, gazing at the saint's face. [1] If my saint goes hungry, I too go hungry; if the saint eats, I eat; where my saint sleeps, there I stay awake, and I play within the saint. [2] All places of pilgrimage rest at the feet of my saints, and Lakshmi herself is their maidservant; desire, anger, greed, attachment, and delusion — all four serve them as attendants. [3] Kabir says, listen, O saints — this is the very word spoken by God's own mouth, the greatness of the saint that God sang to Narada in the raga Sarang in the Pancharatra. [4])

Das Kabirji explains: God said to Narada, "O Narada, the saints are dearer to me than my own life. Those who worship me with mind, speech, and action do not return again into the cycle of birth and death. I do not dwell in Vaikunth, nor in Dwarka — but wherever my saint sings devotional songs, I dance there, watching his face, delighting in him. If my saint is hungry, I too am hungry; when the saint eats, I eat. Where my saint sleeps, I stay awake, and I sport within the saint. All the places of pilgrimage rest at my saint's feet, and Lakshmiji is the saint's maidservant; desire, anger, greed, attachment, and delusion — all four serve him diligently." Kabirji says: listen, O saints — this is the very speech spoken directly from God's own mouth, which God spoke to Narada in the Pancharatra while describing the saint's glory.

Raga Ramgri:

_Maru Vrindavan chhe rudu re, Vaikunth nahi aavu,
nahi aavu Nandjina Lal, nahi aavu. (tek)
Besine rehvu ne tagtag jovu, nahi khavu nahi pivu re - Vaikunth nahi._ ||1||
_Vaiman moklo to moklo vehlu, hun aavish sauna pahelu re - Vaikunth nahi._ ||2||
_Brahmana lokto chhe ati kuda, vaasi Vrajna ruda re - Vaikunth nahi._ ||3||
_Je Vije be poliya hata, tene tatkshan melya kahadi re - Vaikunth nahi._ ||4||
_Narsaiyacho swami antarjami, tame sambhalne Sarangpani re - Vaikunth nahi._ ||5||

(My Vrindavan is lovely — I will not come to Vaikunth, I will not come, O beloved son of Nand, I will not come. [Refrain] There one must only sit and stare fixedly, with nothing to eat and nothing to drink — I will not come to Vaikunth. [1] If you send a heavenly chariot for me, send it quickly — I shall be the very first to come — I will not come to Vaikunth. [2] The worlds of Brahma are utterly false and hollow; the dwellers of Vraj are the true and lovely ones — I will not come to Vaikunth. [3] The two doorkeepers who stood there [Jay and Vijay] were at once thrown out — I will not come to Vaikunth. [4] O Lord of Narsaiyo, knower of all hearts — hear this, O Sarangpani [Krishna] — I will not come to Vaikunth. [5])

Once the cowherd boys insistently urged Lord Krishna, saying, "O Kanuda, you are our special friend — won't you show us your Vaikunth-dham? People praise Vaikunth so highly that we too have grown eager to see such a fine abode." Shri Krishna replied, "Oh, there's nothing there worth seeing, nothing enjoyable." But the cowherd boys, having grown tempted by hearing everyone extol Vaikunth, said, "Come now, friend! Being our special friend and yet hiding your own abode from us — that isn't right." There, he appeared four-armed, in his Chaturbhuj form, utterly inactive, engaged in no activity whatsoever, and without a trace of joy or exuberance. Seeing this dry, joyless atmosphere, the cowherd boys said, "Hey Krishna, where is Radha here? Where is the curd, where is the butter?" Then the Lord said, "Here dwell those who have attained moksha and been granted liberation, so there is no milk, curd, or butter here — those are found only in the land of Vraj." Seeing such a bland place, the disheartened cowherd boys, disappointed, said they did not care for this Vaikunth at all — they found Vrindavan far dearer. Narsinh Mehta composed a pada about this in the raga Ramgri (given above).

The cowherd boys say to Lord Krishna: "O beloved Krishna of Nandji, our own Vrindavan feels far dearer to us, so I shall not come to Vaikunth — for there, one must simply sit doing nothing at all, staring fixedly, with nothing whatsoever to eat or drink. So if you send a heavenly chariot to fetch us, send it quickly, so that I may be the very first to board it and come to your Vraj-dham. The people of this universe are exceedingly deceitful, while the residents of Vraj are truly excellent and lovely. From Vaikunth, two gatekeepers named Jay and Vijay were once thrown out. Narsinh Mehta's Lord Vishnu knows the innermost heart, so please accept my wish to come to Vraj."

_Vrindavan aur Vaikunthku, tolyo Tulsidas, bhari so nicho raha, halko gayo aakash_ (Tulsidas weighed Vrindavan and Vaikunth on a scale: the heavier one stayed low, and the lighter one rose up into the sky.)

Tulsidasji says: when devotees of God weighed Vrindavan and Vaikunth, the one that was heavier — Vrindavan — remained down here on earth, while Vaikunth, being the lighter one, had its pan rise up high into the sky.

_Karm chhape Vaikunth manhe, sarge bhelabhel, satjug sab gaye Jivana, kaljug lebe mail._ ||63|| (Ritual karma lies hidden within Vaikunth, and in heaven it is mingled everywhere; all of it departed in Satyug, but Kaliyug takes on its taint.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: devotees banished ritual observance (karmakand) into exile, and that karma hid itself away within Vaikunth, while in the heavenly realms karma became mixed into everything; and looking at Satyug, Dwapar, and all the other ages, it crept into japa, tapa, pilgrimage, vows, mantra recitation, spiritual practice, sacrifice, and the like. But in Kaliyug, devotees who practise single-minded devotion have driven it out entirely, banishing it into exile and casting it aside.

_Vaikunth laago rovane, sarag rahyo sir koot, taak sevak Jivana, ham beechme leene loot._ ||64|| (Vaikunth took to weeping, and heaven remained beating its head; look, O servant Jivan — we have plundered them right in the middle.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: Vaikunth was the abode for devotees of the heavenly realms who practised devotion through ritual and religious observance; devotees like us, who practise single-minded devotion, forcibly turned them back midway through true teaching. Thus we plundered, midway, the devotees of Vaikunth and the heavenly realms — and so poor Vaikunth began to grieve, and — as the passage itself repeats — we plundered the devotees of the heavenly realms midway, and so poor Vaikunth began to grieve, while the heavenly realms, despite making the most desperate efforts, striking their heads in anguish, grew utterly despondent and fell into deep sorrow.

_Kaha karau vaikunth hi jaay? Jahan nahi Nand, jahan na Jashoda, nahi jahan Gopi-Gwal, na gaay. Jahan nahi jal Jamunako nirmal, aur nahi kadamnaki thaant. Parmanand Prabhu chatur gwalini, Vraj-raj taji meri jaay balaay_ (What use is it even to go to Vaikunth? There is no Nand there, no Jashoda, no gopis or cowherds, not even cows; there is no pure water of the Yamuna, and no shade of the kadamba trees. Says Parmanand: the clever gopi declares — may my ill fate go wherever it will, rather than that I forsake the dust of Vraj.)

Revered Yadunath, on the occasion of Puniyad's Janmashtami — Monday, 12 August 1963 (Samvat 2019, Shravan Krishna 8) — distributed to the devotees present a booklet titled Prarthana ane Prasadi as a gift; the above pada of Parmanandji appears on page 2 of that booklet.

Jagdish notebook no. 122, Damodar Ramdas notebook no. 2, page 19.

Ramkabir pada:

_Vraj vahalu re - Vaikunth nahi aavu (2)
tyan Nandkuvar kyanthi lavu re - Vraj
tyan lalit tribhangi nathi Girdhari (2)
sange soi-e Radhapyari (2)
emne nirkhta ankh thare mari re - Vraj
tyan Jumna Shri Girdhar chhe ja nahi (2)
maru man tyan satya thare ja nahi (2)
mara pran prasanna tyan rahe ja nahi re - Vraj
tyan Shri Vrindavan raas nahi (2)
Vrajvanitani sange vilas nahi
Vishnu venu vayano adhyas nahi re - Vraj
sukh swargnu Krishna vina kadvu (2)
mane na game Brahma sadan adavu re (2)
dhik dhik e sukh paamine padvu re - Vraj_

(Vraj is dear to me — I will not come to Vaikunth. Where would I find Nandji's son there? There is no graceful, thrice-bent Girdhari there, with beloved Radha resting at his side — beholding them is what cools my eyes. There is no Yamuna, no Shri Girdhar there; my mind finds no true rest there; my very breath is not at peace there. There is no raas-dance of Vrindavan there, no delight in the company of Vraj's women, no absorption in the sound of Vishnu's flute. Heavenly pleasure without Krishna is bitter; I do not like that bare, empty abode of Brahma — shame, shame on attaining such a joy only to fall from it.)

The clever gopi says: "Oh, what would I do by going to Vaikunth? What benefit is there in going to Vaikunth? For there is no Nandji there, nor Jashodaji, no gopis, no cowherds, not even cows; moreover there is no pure water of the Yamuna, nor the shade of the kadamba tree." Thus says Parmanand: the clever gopi declares that if any ill fate must befall her for forsaking Vraj, let it go elsewhere — if misfortune must come to her, she would rather it choose some other place.

_Sukh seja shital mahel, samukh sahaj bataai, kahai Kabir Vaikunthki, aas karai balaai._ ||21|| (A comfortable bed, a cool palace, and other such delights lie readily displayed before us — says Kabir, only one whose fate is to come to ruin would still long to attain Vaikunth.)

Das Kabirji says: leaving behind such an abode where comforts like a pleasing bed and a cooling palace are shown to us readily and effortlessly, only one destined for misfortune would still hope to attain that Vaikunth.

_Sarag narak nahi vanchhahi, aur Vaikunth Kailas, Chaturbhujdas darshan Ramka, paavai tabahi das._ ||11|| (Only when a devotee desires neither heaven nor hell, nor even Vaikunth or Kailas, does that servant — says Chaturbhujdas — attain the vision of Ram.)

Chaturbhujdas says: whoever harbours no desire to attain heaven or the splendour of hell, and also has no wish to obtain Vaikunth or Kailas, only such a devotee then attains the vision (darshan) of Ram.

_Narayanaparah sarve na kutashchana bibhyati, swargapavarganakeshvapi tulyarthadarshinah_ (Those devoted wholly to Narayan fear nothing whatsoever; they regard heaven, liberation, and hell alike, seeing them as equal in worth.) _Narayanparayan nihsang bhakt hai, vahan na narakse darta hai, na swargki iccha karta hai, aur na moksh hi chahta hai_ (A devotee devoted single-heartedly to Narayan, unattached to anything, neither fears hell, nor desires heaven, nor even longs for liberation.)

In the chapter on the grace bestowed upon Naranadas, the Samagam writes about Vaikunth: the Gokul-lila was established in the Dwapar age. In the Satyug and Treta ages, the Lord of Grace (Kripanath) resided in Vaikunth; in this Dwapar age he came to Shri Gokul, locking up Vaikunth behind him as he left. For this reason, the charming flute-player Lord is the true one; even Vaikunth could not prove itself supremely accomplished — that is, it could not establish God's rightful, true nature as its own possessor.

Adhyaru Maharaj writes, in the Prithvi Dhol, verse 8:

_Var chalyo Vaikunth ufaro, te pad siyal agamya e._ ||12|| _Pohoto var param pad mandir aapane, jaha rajaji Hari Parabrahm e._ ||13|| (The bridegroom set off, turning away from Vaikunth, toward that peaceful, unattainable state; he arrived at his own supreme abode, where Rajaji Hari, the Supreme Brahman, resides.)

The wedded Husband, the Supreme Brahman, set out toward his own abode — his own primeval Vrindavan-dham, situated above Vaikunth, supreme above all, beyond even the realms of Janalok and Tamalok. Understanding the greatness of that abode is exceedingly difficult for anyone. This Husband, the Supreme Brahman, arrived at his own most excellent mansion, the abode of which he himself, Lord Parabrahm, is the very master.

Sadguru Jivandasji Maharaj, in the couplets (sakhis) of the 21 Angas, as well as in the sakhis on the union of Name and Form, has presented Vaikunth in many different ways.

_Tan man arpe Ramku, to de Vaikunthko dham, guru charane arpe Jivana, to charan kamal vishram._ ||31|| (Offer body and mind to Ram, and he grants the abode of Vaikunth; but offer them, O Jivan, at the Guru's feet, and he grants rest at his own lotus feet.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: if you surrender everything to God, he grants you a dwelling in the abode of Vaikunth. But if you accept surrender at the Guru's feet, he grants you the bliss of dwelling in God's own abode and serving him there.

_Mel mugat bhai Jivana, jab sadguru diyo updesh, sarag narak Vaikunthlu, jyu haar upaade kesh._ ||82|| (Liberation from all bondage came, O Jivan, when the Sadguru gave his teaching — heaven, hell, and Vaikunth were plucked away like hair pulled out in a fit of anger.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: when the Sadguru made clear the truth about Ram and Kabir, and gave the realization of the oneness between the two imperishable syllables (aksharas), then, as if in anger, like hair torn out from the head, the web of illusion woven of heaven, hell, and the rest was cast off and flung away.

_Swarg nagar dono taje, nahi Vaikunthki aas, Ramnaam bhaj Jivana, jahan sadguru shabd vishwas._ ||108|| (Forsake both the city of heaven and hope of Vaikunth — chant Ram's name, O Jivan, and place your faith in the Sadguru's word.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: if you are to walk only by placing faith in the Sadguru's teaching, then hold that faith and trust, abandon all thoughts of the higher or lower realms, whether heaven or hell, and, without any desire to attain even Vaikunth, simply chant the name of Ram.

_Ham jaanyo Hari dhunkdo, Vaikunth peli paar, vebhi nedo Jivana, jo sadguru hoy kripal._ ||143|| (We had thought Hari to be far off, beyond Vaikunth on the other shore; but he is nearer still, O Jivan, if the Sadguru turns gracious.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: we used to think that God dwelt very far away, on the distant far shore of Vaikunth, separate from this earthly world. But if the Sadguru's grace descends, he is found even nearer than that, right here in this very world.

_Sant darshanku Jivana, aash kare Vaikunth, Vaikunth bapareki kaha chali, jo vanchhe Kamlakanth._ ||7|| (Even Vaikunth longs, O Jivan, for the sight of a saint — what power has poor Vaikunth, when even the Lord of Lakshmi himself yearns for it?)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: even Vaikunth keeps longing for the sight of a saint. Alas, what power does poor Vaikunth have — even the Lord of Vaikunth, Lakshmi's own husband, keeps longing for it too.

_Nirvasik je Jivana, Harijan taaka naam, sarag narak Vaikunth taj, te samre Sitaram._ ||16|| (Whoever is free of all desire, O Jivan, that alone is the true name of a devotee of Hari — forsaking desire for heaven, hell, or Vaikunth, he keeps remembering Sitaram.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: whoever is free of all worldly cravings, that alone is worthy of the name "devotee of Hari" (harijan); he forsakes the cravings for heaven, hell, and Vaikunth, and continually keeps remembering Sitaram.

_Kotik Vaikunth upre, Shri Vrindavan sukh dham, taathe neeki Jivana, sant sangat vishram._ ||30|| (Above tens of millions of Vaikunths stands Shri Vrindavan, the abode of joy — but better still, O Jivan, is rest found in the company of saints.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: more than crores of Vaikunths, Shri Vrindavan is the abode that gives God greater joy; and greater joy still than that lies in taking rest in the company of saints.

_Aag jalo Vaikunthma, jahan sant samagam nahi, taathe neeki Jivana, Shri Bansivatki chhanhi._ ||31|| (Let Vaikunth burn in fire, where the company of saints cannot be found — better, O Jivan, is the shade of the sacred Bansivat.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: let Vaikunth burn and be destroyed by fire, if the company of saints cannot be found there; better than that is to dwell in the shade of the Bansivat tree.

_Aag jalo Vaikunthme, jahan sant samagam nahi, bhagat viyoge dukhiyo bhayo, uhan jan to aave nahi._ ||32|| (Let Vaikunth burn, where the company of saints cannot be found — the Lord grew sorrowful there for want of his devotees, for no devotee ever comes there.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: let that Vaikunth, where the company of saints cannot be found, burn and be destroyed by fire — for there, God grew sorrowful from separation from his devotees, because devotees of Hari never go there.

_Mai Gokulma vaas vasu, kabhu Shesh sukhasan dham, kabhu ek Vaikunth Jivana, kabhu nagar Ayodhya dham._ ||36|| (I make my true dwelling in Gokul; yet at times I dwell in the blissful abode upon Shesh's couch, sometimes, O Jivan, in Vaikunth, and sometimes in the town of Ayodhya.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: God declares, "I dwell permanently in Gokul; but in another form, at times I stay in the blissful abode of the Kshirsagar, upon Sheshnag's couch, and at times in Vaikunth, and at times in the town of Ayodhya."

_Sir Sanakadik Jivana, chhoda Vaikunth manhi, sant sangat sapne nahi, to parampad kaise paay._ ||65|| (Even the great Sanakadik, O Jivan, were left behind within Vaikunth — never even in dream did they keep the company of saints, so how then could they attain the supreme state?)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: misfortune befell even the Sanakadik sages, being left within Vaikunth, because they had never, even in a dream, kept the company of saints — so how, then, could they ever attain the supreme state?

_Aadha mata kaun kaamka, jo paave Vaikunthko dham, taathe jagat bhali Jivana, kabahu sant sangat vishram._ ||73|| (What use is a half-finished creed that only wins one the abode of Vaikunth? Better, O Jivan, is this world, where one may sometimes find rest in the company of saints.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: what use is such a half-hearted, incomplete devotion to God — devoid of service to saints — that only wins, by its merit, the mere attainment of Vaikunth-dham? Better than that is reckoned this worldly life, for in it one can at least sometimes find the chance to rest in the company of saints.

_Mukh maru ta daasko, ninda kare jo koy, Vaikunththi daarahu, Jivan yu barad mohe._ ||136|| (Whoever speaks ill of that servant, I shall strike him on the mouth — this is my vow, O Jivan, even should I have to reach into Vaikunth to do it.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: God declares, "Whether they are devotees of Shiv, Brahma, or the other gods, like Ravan and his kind — if they speak ill of devotion to me or of my devotees, or grow jealous of them, then, without fear or shame of them, I will speak to them plainly, straight to their face. And wherever they may be — Vaikunth, Shivlok, Brahmalok, or anywhere else — if they speak such ill words, I will threaten them and make them stop speaking. That is my vow; that is my rule."

_Ved katebthi Jivana, nyare Harike das, swarg narak Vaikunth taj, kare Hari charanki aash._ ||154|| (Free from the Vedas and the Book, O Jivan, are Hari's true devotees — forsaking heaven, hell, and Vaikunth, they hold hope only in Hari's feet.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: God's exclusive devotees remain indifferent to the ritual observances prescribed by the Vedas, Puranas, or the Quran. Renouncing heaven and the rest, they hold their hope in taking refuge only at God's lotus feet.

_Vaikunth chhanhi Jivana, nyare Harike das, sol-kalasu shaamlo, sakal sevak sukh dham._ ||33|| (Leaving Vaikunth behind, O Jivan, Hari's true devotee is set apart — the dark Lord, full of sixteen powers, becomes the abode of joy for all his servants.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: God set his intent on leaving Vaikunth behind and dwelling in the village of Gokul instead. That Lord Krishna is endowed with sixteen kalas (perfections). Gokul is that pure, blissful village which gives joy to all devotees; there he resolved to dwell.

_Pahela dash avatar hai, dooja Vaikunth jaan, treejo Omkar Jivana, chautha ghatghat maan._ ||5|| (First are the ten avatars; know the second to be Vaikunth; the third, O Jivan, is Omkar; and the fourth is the one dwelling in every heart.)

Jivandasji Maharaj, listing the seven honest-looking thieves, says: first, the ten avatars are the honest thief; know the second to be Vaikunth; the third is Omkar; and the fourth thief is the one who calls the divine dwelling in every heart the complete Parabrahm — that too, believe my word, is an honest-looking thief.

_Sar Sanakadik Jivana, chhodo Vaikunth manhe, Sitapati bhootal vase, sant samagam manhe._ ||22|| (The great Sanakadik, O Jivan, were left resting within Vaikunth — but Sitapati [Ram] dwells here on earth, wherever the company of saints takes place.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: great sages like Sanakadik were left behind to rest within the abode of Vaikunth, left there still seeking God — but Sitapati Ram dwells here on this earth, wherever the gathering of saints takes place.

_Darshan karan doheli, biraha Vaikunth manhi, ko ek Harijan mile Jivana, ham baithe taaki chhanhi._ ||9|| (In Vaikunth, [God] suffers the anguish of separation, for it is hard to find a sight of loving devotees there — should even a single devotee of Hari be found, O Jivan, there I sit in his shade.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: loving saints and devotees do not go to Vaikunth, so it is hard to obtain their darshan there; God, growing restless with the pain of that separation, seeks the sight of his loving devotees, and should even one devotee-saint be found on earth, I dwell in his company.

_Mai Vaikunthvasi Jivana, bohot rahyo udaas, Vrindavanki kunjma, Radhe sang vilas._ ||298|| (I, as a dweller of Vaikunth, O Jivan, remained deeply sorrowful — but in the groves of Vrindavan, in play with Radha, joy was found.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: God declares, "When I dwelt in Vaikunth, even though I had one such as Lakshmi to serve at my feet, my heart remained sorrowful. But when I sported with Radha in the groves of Vrindavan, I became joyful — I found the essence of love through Radha's company."

_Mai Vaikunthvasi Jivana, sab santanke viyog, Vrindavan sada rahu, bhav bhagat ras bhog._ ||299|| (I, dwelling in Vaikunth, O Jivan, suffered separation from all the saints; now I dwell forever in Vrindavan, enjoying the essence of loving, devoted worship.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: God declares, "I used to dwell in Vaikunth, but there I bore the sorrow of separation from all saints. So now I dwell always in Vrindavan, where I find the good fortune of relishing the essence of loving devotion and its tender delight."

_Kabir sant darshan van doheli, brahoni Vaikunth manhi, Ram Kabira jo mile, ham varte taaki chhanhi._ ||300|| (Kabir says: without the sight of a saint, that delight is hard to attain — its playing-ground lies within Vaikunth's expanse; but wherever Ram and the devotee-saint Kabir can be found together, there we abide, sheltered in that shade.)

Das Kabirji says: without the sight of a saint, the enjoyment of the tender delight of loving devotion is hard to attain. Its play-ground lies within Vaikunth, but if Lord Ram and the devotee-saint Kabir can be found together somewhere, we would rather remain, submissive, under their shelter.

_Kabir Ram bulava bhejiya, Kabire dino roy, jo sukh hai sant hil mil, so Vaikunth na hoy._ ||301|| (Kabir wept when Ram sent his summons — for the joy found in the fellowship of saints, mingled together, is not to be found in Vaikunth.)

Das Kabirji says: when the summons of God comes to one who has been in the company of saints, it brings deep sorrow — because the joy of intimate fellowship, gathering, and devotional worship found together with saints in satsang is not to be found in Vaikunth.

_Kabir mera man pankhi bhaya, ud gaya aakash, Vaikunth to khaali bhaya, Saheb santo paas._ ||305|| (Kabir: my mind became a bird and flew up into the sky; but Vaikunth was found empty — the Lord dwells near his saints.)

Das Kabirji says: in search of God, my mind flew up into the sky, like a bird, to Vaikunth — but Vaikunth lay empty of God; God dwells only near his saints.

_Sapt puripe Jivana, Vaikunthpe ati saar, Vrindavan sohamnu, jahan Radhe sang vihar._ ||306|| (Above the seven sacred cities, and above Vaikunth too, O Jivan, stands supreme the lovely Vrindavan, where God sports together with Radha.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: far more excellent than the seven sacred cities, and even more excellent than Vaikunth, is the surpassing, beautiful Vrindavan, where God sports together with Radha.

_Vaikunth chhodi Jivana, aayo Gokul manhi, Vrajsukh to tahan sapne nahi, mope rahyo na jaay._ ||311|| (Leaving Vaikunth, O Jivan, I came to Gokul — for even in dream, no joy like that of Vraj is found there, and so I could not remain.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: God declares, "I left Vaikunth and came into Gokul, because there the joy of Vraj is not found even in dream, and so I could not bear to stay there."

_Kabir nishkami nirmal dasha, pakde chaare khoote, kahe Kabir ta daaski, aash kare Vaikunth._ ||316|| (One free of all desire, dwelling in a pure state, holding firm on all four sides — says Kabir, even Vaikunth longs for such a devotee to come to it.)

Das Kabirji says: whoever is free of all desire, dwells in a state of pure devotion, and remains steadfast and unmoved on every side — even Vaikunth longs and hopes that such a devotee might one day come to it.

_Prahlad bichara kaha kare, kamanki dhundi naah, naame baaho Jivana, chhodo Vaikunth manh._ ||366|| (Poor Prahlad — what could he do, having found no bow of grace? Clinging only to the Name, O Jivan, he was sent away from Vaikunth.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: poor Prahlad was helpless — what could he do? He held no ill will at all toward God's Name or toward a Guru, in seeking the devotion of Name-and-Form through a Sadguru. But it was not possible for him to find one, so he clung only to God's Name — and for that, God sent him to his own abode.

Ghat-Ghatna (The One Dwelling in Every Heart) — In the Samagam, in the chapter on the Brahman of the world (maya), the second sakhi of the Garbhavali Anga is given, where it says: the thief who dwells in every heart means committing wrongful acts while believing oneself to possess the knowledge of Brahman.

_Mansa Devi ushni, taathe bhayo Omkar, ghatghat vyapak Jivana, so khole Nandadwar._ ||2|| (The Goddess Mansa arose, and from her came Omkar; that which pervades every heart, O Jivan, is the one who opens the door of Nand's house.)

Jivandasji Maharaj, in the Anga called Garbhavali (the wheel of the 84 lakh species of birth, in which the soul wanders entangled), says: at the beginning of creation, the illusory goddess named Mansa arose, and from her the Omkar-imbued (three-gunas) creation came forth. That very Supreme Being, whose essence pervades every single body in the world — that same Supreme Being sports in the courtyard of Nandji.

_Brahmagyani anusare, ghatghat vyapak Ram, hamare yu vrat Jivana, je Sitapatiko naam._ ||5|| (Those who know Brahman follow the Ram who pervades every heart — but our vow, O Jivan, is this: devotion only to the Name of Sitapati.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: those learned in the knowledge of Brahman, aspiring to know Brahman, worship with a spiritual sentiment the Ram who pervades every single limb of every heart. But our own rule is this: to worship only that name which is Sitapati Ram's name.

_Ghatghatma Hari lekhve, aape ho rahyo Brahm, meede hato Jivana, te shir par leeno karm._ ||15|| (Reckoning that Hari pervades every heart, one takes oneself to be Brahman — but O Jivan, one who was already effaced thereby draws that bondage of karma upon his own head.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: convinced that God pervades everyone and everything, a person sets out to become Brahman himself. But by doing so, he brings upon his own head a bondage of karma that had, in truth, no real existence at all.

_Jyu jalme pratibimb hai, tyu ghatghat vyapak Ram, guru prasade Jivana, paaiye mool Chandrako dhaam._ ||16|| (As a reflection falls in water, so does Ram, pervading every heart; by the Guru's grace, O Jivan, may we attain the true moon itself, not merely its reflection.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: just as the reflection of an object falls in water, so too does the reflected image of Lord Ram fall within every single heart. But through the Guru's grace, instead of settling for that reflection, we shall attain the true moon itself — Lord Ram, the real, original moon.

_Sanya seti Jivana, kabahu na kije rosh, aape ghatghat le rahyo, aape banayo dhosh._ ||17|| (Never grow angry with the Lord, O Jivan, nor resentful — he himself dwells within every heart by his own will, and he himself has set this whole universe running.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: never grow angry with God, never bring resentment or ill will against him, nor sulk against him — for God himself, of his own accord, is dwelling within every heart, and he himself has set this entire universe in motion.

_Ghatghat to Hari lekhve, pan sanya santo paas, dhua dharhar Jivana, taame kaiso baas._ ||19|| (We may reckon that Hari pervades every heart, but the Lord who is near his saints is different — like grasping at billowing smoke, O Jivan, what true dwelling could there be in that?)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: we understand that God pervades every heart — but that is Maryada Purushottam (the Lord bound by cosmic limits), whereas the God who is near his saints is Purna Purushottam, the complete, unbounded Lord. Just as one might try to grasp handfuls of billowing smoke, yet the supreme essence could never truly dwell within that smoke, so too is it futile to strive to grasp the God-in-every-heart as though grasping at smoke.

_Ko kahe Hari soon aakashme, ko kahe Hari ghatghat manhi, sadguru bataayo Jivana, Shri Bansivatki chhanhi._ ||78|| (Some say Hari dwells in the empty sky, some say Hari dwells within every heart; but the Sadguru showed, O Jivan, the shade of the sacred Bansivat.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: among those of differing opinions, some say that God resides in the empty void of the sky, while others say God resides everywhere, within every single body — but the Sadguru showed that God, in his true form, resides at the sacred Bansivat.

_Ghatghat vyapak Jivana, pan Antaryami ek, mai balihari ta daaski, jahan sadguru shabd vivek._ ||120|| (God pervades every heart, O Jivan — yet the indwelling Witness is one alone; I offer myself in devotion to that servant, wherever the Sadguru's word brings true discernment.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: the indwelling God, the Antaryami, pervades every single body everywhere. Yet that divine essence is but one alone; blessed, therefore, are those devotees who worship while placing their faith in the Sadguru's teaching — God himself declares, "I sacrifice myself for such devotees."

_Sadguru samjhaayo Jivana, gupt pragat je baat, ek roop ghatghat vase, ek Sitapati Raghunath._ ||121|| (The Sadguru explained, O Jivan, the truth both hidden and manifest — one form dwells within every heart, yet the one true Lord is Sitapati Raghunath.)
